sections.text:
1 Maxime dolendum est hoc fragmentum librarii pigritia interiisse. Solum fere
olim ex libris supererat Barbilli celeberrimi astrologi, qui tempore Vespasiani
imperatoris florebat; vide Friedländer, Sittengeschichte, I, p. 132-133. Cf. cod.
Paris. 2506, f. 80r.
sections.en: 1 It is greatly to be lamented that this fragment has perished through the laziness of the scribe. It was almost the only thing that formerly survived from the books of Barbillus, the very famous astrologer, who flourished in the time of the emperor Vespasian; see Friedländer, Sittengeschichte, I, p. 132-133. Cf. cod. Paris. 2506, f. 80r.

summary.headline: Astrological Chapters 79–96
summary.text: Astrological chapter catalogue entries 79–96, covering planting by the Moon’s culmination, planetary theorems, death in a nativity, stations, falling away, death timing, inceptions, lunar degrees by zodiacal sign, failure, rumor, success, civil war, outcomes, profit, and receipt of property. The notes cite Barbillus, Heliodorus, Dorotheus, and Leontius, with cross-references to Taurin and Venetian codices.
